name: Sika ViscoCrete-88 SC
paste:
SIKA® VISCOCRETE®-88 SC: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC, May 2023, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sika-viscocrete-88sc.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description. Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC is a liquid high-range water reducing and workability retaining admixture for concrete and shotcrete that requires extended workability.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Applications that require high quality concrete
    - Applications that require improved workability retention
    - Self compacting concrete
    - Ideal for shotcrete

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: HIGH-RANGE WATER REDUCING CONCRETE ADMIXTURE WITH WORKABILITY RETAINING TECHNOLOGY
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates. Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC meets the requirements of AS1478.1 (type HWR).
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS1478.1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Extended slump retention
    - Less sensitive to variations in cement and aggregate types
    - Improved cohesion properties
    - Improved early and ultimate strengths
    - Improved rheology and durability
    - Reduced drying shrinkage
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Modified polycarboxylate in aqueous solution
    - Appearance and colour: Light straw colour liquid
    - Density: 1.05 kg/l (at +20°C)
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 10 litre container; 1000 litre IBC bulk deliveries
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production if stored properly in undamaged containers.
    - Storage conditions: Store in dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +35°C. Protect from direct sunlight and frost.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2023, Version 01.01) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2023, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Recommended dosage: Recommended dosage for concrete: 400 ml to 1500 ml per 100 kg of total cementitious material. Optimum dosage should be determined by site trials.
4.3 Dispensing.
    - Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC should be dispensed through suitable calibrated dosing equipment with the mixing water
    - The standard rules of good concreting practice, concerning production as well as placing, are to be followed. Refer to relevant standards.
    - Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC should not be added to dry cement .
4.4 Compatibility. Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC can be used in conjunction with all the concrete admixtures manufactured by Sika Australia PTY Limited with the exclusion of Sikament ® NN. All admixtures must be added separately. For additional information, please contact Sika technical personnel.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2023, Version 01.01) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC, May 2023, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sika-viscocrete-88sc.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® ViscoCrete®-88 SC, version 23/03/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/sds-sika-viscocrete-88sc.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
